title: Dedicated Capacity: Procurement-Ready Value Framework
content:
Purpose
This brief is a procurement-ready value framework for Redwood’s Dedicated capacity offering. It combines buyer-facing messaging, a negotiation scorecard, quick rebuttals to common procurement/legal/finance objections, and sample contract language for SLA/credit mechanics. Target audiences: platform architects, procurement teams, CFO/finance owners, and security/compliance stakeholders evaluating reserved GPU commitments.

Executive summary (1-paragraph)
For customers who need predictable throughput, strict data isolation, and contractual uptime/latency guarantees, Redwood Dedicated packages reserved GPU pools, network isolation, and SLA-backed economics into a single procurement-friendly offering. Instead of treating capacity as a variable operating expense with unpredictable performance, Redwood Dedicated converts core inference workloads into a predictable, contract-backed line item with operational controls (autoscale policies, burst windows), observability, and a clear remediation/credit path.

Positioning pillars (short bullets for decks)
- Predictable throughput: committed GPU units + throughput SLOs measured at route-level (tokens/sec and concurrent requests).
- Isolation & compliance: physical tenant isolation and customer-managed VPC options for regulatory requirements.
- Commercial certainty: usage discounts for reserved capacity, transparent overage pricing, and SLA credit mechanics.
- Operationally owned: Redwood provides runbooks, playbooks, and a named escalation engineer for onboarding and go-live.
- Cost control levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles tuned for the customer workload.

Buyer personas & what matters to them
- Platform Architect: cares about deterministic latency/throughput, autoscale behavior, integration with internal load balancers. Wants technical metrics, capacity planning templates, and test harnesses.
- Procurement Lead: wants clear billing cadence, commitment duration options, and termination/exit terms. Focus: predictable spend and legal risk.
- Finance/CFO: unit economics, ROI, and breakpoints vs public cloud variable spend. Wants an apples-to-apples TCO comparison and amortization guidance.
- Security/Compliance Officer: data residency, audit logs, and KMS/HSM compatibility. Wants architecture diagrams and SOC/ISO artifacts.

Key metrics we commit to (how to present in RFP/contract)
- Throughput SLO: % of requests achieving median and tail tokens/sec thresholds measured weekly per route.
- Latency SLO: p50/p95/p99 response time targets for typical prompt sizes and streaming scenarios.
- Availability SLA: % uptime for the Dedicated cluster control plane and inference API (defined by region and maintenance windows).
- Capacity assurance: guaranteed GPU count available for provisioning within X minutes; burst windows for Y% above baseline.
- Observability: retention and access to token-level cost/latency metrics for Z days.

Procurement scorecard (sales-facing negotiation checklist)
- Commitment term: 12 / 24 / 36 month options with escalating discounts.
- Minimum baseline: define guaranteed GPU units and how they map to vCPU/GPU SKU equivalence.
- Burst policy: specify burstable capacity, eligible windows, and price for bursts.
- SLA credits: arithmetic for credits (example: 5% monthly credit for availability below SLA). Cap on credits and cure period.
- Data handling: VPC connectivity, encryption-at-rest, access to audit logs, and optional on-prem package.
- Exit & migration: assistance in model state export, prefix-cache evacuation, and model weights transfer within an agreed runbook window.
- Change control: process for adding/removing capacity and rolling upgrades.

Common procurement objections + recommended responses
- "We can just use CSP-managed endpoints and scale elastically."
  Rebuttal: CSP endpoints expose variability in latency and cold-start behavior; Dedicated guarantees baseline throughput and offers predictable unit economics for sustained workloads. We include test harnesses to validate SLA behavior before signing.
- "We already self-host inference — why buy committed capacity?"
  Rebuttal: Self-hosting transfers full operational risk and engineering burden to your team. Redwood Dedicated combines a hardened runtime, observability, and a contractual SLA so your team can reallocate engineering effort to product differentiation. We also provide on-prem integration paths if full self-hosting is required.
- "What about cost if utilization drops?"
  Rebuttal: Contract terms include burst and overage mechanisms plus a roadmap for seasonal flexibility (e.g., swap windows, temporary scale-down credits) to avoid stranded spend. We can model a blended TCO and propose phased commitments tied to usage milestones.
- "How do we trust the SLA measurement?"
  Rebuttal: Measurements are derived from per-request telemetry and token-level tracing accessible to the customer through the console or via secure export. We sign measurement definitions into the SOW and provide periodic reports.

Competitive differentiation (short matrix narrative)
- CSP-managed endpoints: Strength = elasticity and integrated billing. Weakness = high tail latency variance, opaque kernel/quantization choices, no commitment-backed throughput guarantee. Redwood differentiates with committed throughput, observability, and explicit fallback policies to lower-cost model variants.
- Open-source/self-hosted stacks: Strength = control and no vendor lock. Weakness = engineering cost, debugging, and ops overhead. Redwood’s value is transferring operational burden while preserving customer control via private deployment options and model/version pinning.
- Specialist inference vendors: Strength = performance tuning; Weakness = limited deployment modes and weaker enterprise procurement experience. Redwood pairs inference performance with a PLG-driven developer experience and procurement playbook tailored for enterprise legal/finance.

Sample SLA language (snippets for legal)
- Availability: "Redwood will ensure that Dedicated inference endpoints are available 99.90% of each calendar month excluding scheduled maintenance windows and agreed outage windows. If Redwood fails to meet the Availability SLA in a calendar month, customer will be eligible for a service credit equal to X% of the monthly Dedicated fee for each 0.1% below the SLA, up to a maximum of Y%."
- Throughput guarantee: "Redwood guarantees a baseline throughput of T tokens/sec aggregate for the contracted cluster under the baseline GPU allocation. Throughput measurements will be calculated from request telemetry aggregated daily. Failure to meet the throughput guarantee for more than N days in a rolling 30-day window will entitle customer to the remedy described in Exhibit B (credits and operational remediation)."
- Measurement & dispute: "Measurement methodology and data access are defined in Exhibit A. Customer and Redwood will meet weekly during the first 90 days post-go-live to validate telemetry. Disputes follow the escalation pathway in the support addendum."

Negotiation levers (what sales can trade)
- Commitment length (12/24/36 months).
- Early-termination carve-outs for M&A/IPO/force majeure.
- Price breakpoints tied to sustained utilization thresholds.
- Project implementation fees (one-time) vs. ramped onboarding credits.
- Longer observability retention or custom dashboarding as an add-on.

Operational checklist to attach to SOW (for engineering/solutions handoff)
- Performance validation plan: synthetic traffic template, representative prompt set, golden latency/throughput targets.
- Onboarding runbook: network/VPC setup, KMS/HSM integration, model packaging guidance, DR/backup plan.
- Escalation path: named customer success lead, solutions engineer, and on-call SRE contact with SLA-backed response times.
- Rollout plan: canary policy, route tagging, automatic fallback to lower-cost variants during pressure.

Customer-facing one-pager for procurement (CFO friendly)
- Headline: Convert variable inference spend into predictable committed capacity with measurable SLAs.
- Financial case: Example: 24-month commit for 10 dedicated GPUs yields X% discount vs. on-demand and reduces per-token cost by Y for steady-state 70% utilization. Includes sample chart: committed vs on-demand spend over 24 months.
- Risk controls: capacity swap windows, short-term burst credits, and a clear exit path for model state export.
- Ask: Sign SOW + 30-day pilot validation period (pilot priced at partial commitment credit).

AE/seller scripts (two-liner snippets)
- To Platform Architect: "We’ll run your prompt set in our sandbox and commit to measurable p95 latency and tokens/sec targets before production — we’ll include the test harness in the SOW so you can validate the results yourself."
- To Procurement: "Think of this as converting your largest inference workloads from a variable cloud line item into a predictable reserved contract with SLA credits and built-in operational support."

Appendix: Sample TCO inputs for a CFO model (what we need from customer)
- Current monthly inference tokens, peak concurrency, p95 latency requirement, current monthly cloud spend, preferred commitment length.
- We return: blended per-token cost under commitment, break-even utilization, recommended commitment size, and suggested ramp schedule.

Next steps (internal)
1) Finalize the Exhibit A/B legal snippets with legal counsel (copy to sales/legal channel).
2) Prepare a TCO spreadsheet template for Solutions Engineering to run live pilots.
3) Build a short one-slide CFR (cost/financial rationale) for AE playbook.
4) Run enablement session for sales and solutions: example negotiations and role plays.

Notes / open questions (working items)
- Define burst window economics more precisely (minutes vs hours).
- Align measurement definitions with telemetry team for auditability.
- Decide default credit cap (Y% in SLA language) and cure period length.
